# Secret Drop -- Full Documentation

> Free, open-source zero-knowledge secret sharing application. Encrypts text and files client-side with AES-256-GCM before transmission -- the server never sees plaintext data or decryption keys.

## Docs

- [Homepage](BASE_URL): Main entry point for creating encrypted secrets. Users type or upload content, the browser encrypts it locally, and generates a shareable self-destructing link. Supports optional passphrase protection, configurable expiration (1 hour to 90 days), single-use mode, and view count limits. No account or registration needed.
- [How It Works](BASE_URL/how-it-works): Detailed technical walkthrough of Secret Drop's zero-knowledge encryption architecture. Explains the 6-step process: key generation, AES-256-GCM encryption in the browser via Web Crypto API, ciphertext transmission, URL fragment key delivery (never sent to server), client-side decryption, and automatic secret destruction. Covers PBKDF2 key derivation with 600,000 SHA-256 iterations for passphrase-protected secrets.
- [Use Cases](BASE_URL/use-cases): Six detailed real-world scenarios with recommended security configurations. Covers: (1) password sharing between team members, (2) confidential document exchange, (3) API key and credential distribution for developers, (4) SSH key transfer, (5) Wi-Fi password sharing, (6) personal information exchange (SSN, medical records). Each scenario includes expiration time and view limit recommendations.
- [FAQ](BASE_URL/faq): Ten frequently asked questions covering: cost (free), account requirements (none), encryption method (AES-256-GCM), data storage location (France), GDPR compliance (by design), open-source license (AGPL-3.0), file size limits (10 MB text, 50,000 characters), secret management via admin links, and the zero-knowledge guarantee that servers cannot access plaintext even under legal compulsion.
- [Legal Notice](BASE_URL/legal-notice): Full legal disclosures including operator identity, hosting provider (OVH Cloud, 2 rue Kellermann, 59100 Roubaix, France), cookie policy (essential technical cookies only, no tracking), GDPR data processing details, and intellectual property information. Built with Laravel framework.
- [Source Code](GITHUB_URL): Complete source code repository under AGPL-3.0 license. Built with Laravel, Alpine.js (CSP build), Tailwind CSS, and Vite. Publicly auditable encryption implementation using the Web Crypto API.

## Security Architecture

- Encryption: AES-256-GCM via Web Crypto API (client-side only)
- Key derivation: PBKDF2 with SHA-256, 600,000 iterations (for passphrase-protected secrets)
- Key transmission: Via URL fragment (#), which browsers never send to servers
- IV: 96 bits (12 bytes), randomly generated per encryption
- Salt: 128 bits (16 bytes), randomly generated per passphrase derivation
- Key size: 256 bits
- Encoding: Base64URL (URL-safe, no padding)
- Double encryption: When a passphrase is used, content is first encrypted with a random key, then encrypted again with the passphrase-derived key
- Token entropy: 128 bits (32 hex characters)
- Magic link tokens: Stored as SHA-256 hashes (plain token sent by email, only hash in database)
- Content Security Policy: Strict CSP with nonce-based inline script/style control
- No unsafe-eval: Alpine.js CSP build used to avoid eval-based XSS vectors
- Server stores: Only ciphertext, IV, salt, and metadata -- never plaintext or keys

## Key Facts

- Created by EDITOR_NAME
- Hosted in France on OVH Cloud servers (2 rue Kellermann, 59100 Roubaix)
- Open source under GNU Affero General Public License v3 (AGPL-3.0)
- Text secrets: up to 50,000 characters
- File secrets: up to 10 MB
- Expiration options: 1 hour, 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days, 90 days
- View limits: single-use or configurable max views (up to 100)
- Available in 11 languages with localized URLs
- No user accounts, no tracking cookies, no third-party analytics
- GDPR compliant by design -- zero-knowledge architecture means no personal data processing
